chunks: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (ra) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from his father from Abi Qutada al-Qummi. He said: Abdullah b. Yahya narrated to us from Aban al-Ahmar from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (as).

He said: The people discussed chivalry (futuwwa) around him, so he said: Do you think that chivalry is immorality and indecency? No! Rather, chivalry and manliness are serving food, giving generously, doing good, and withholding harm. As for that, it is wickedness and immorality.

Then he (as) said: What is manliness? We said: We do not know. He said: Manliness, by Allah, is that a man places his dining table in his courtyard. And manliness is of two kinds: manliness at home and manliness while travelling. As for manliness at home, it is reciting the Quran, adhering to the mosques, walking with the brothers in their needs, and being good to the servant — for it brings joy to the friend and suppresses the enemy. As for manliness while travelling, it is having abundant and good provisions and sharing them with those who are with you, keeping the secrets of the people after you have parted from them, and being light-hearted in a way that does not anger Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Then he (as) said: By Him who sent my grandfather (s) as a true prophet! Surely Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, provides for the servant in proportion to his manliness. Aid descends from the heaven in proportion to his expenditure. And patience descends in proportion to the severity of the affliction.

key_terms.اصطناع المعروف: doing good deeds, performing acts of kindness
key_terms.الفتوة: futuwwa — chivalry or youthful valor, a concept in Islamic ethics denoting noble character traits
key_terms.المروة: muru'a — manliness or magnanimity, encompassing virtuous conduct at home and abroad
key_terms.شطارة: shatara — wickedness or roguishness, contrasted with true chivalry

ai.seo_question: What is the true meaning of chivalry (futuwwa) and manliness (muru'a) in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) corrects a common misconception about futuwwa (chivalry), explaining that true chivalry and muru'a (manliness) consist of generosity, doing good, and withholding harm — not immorality. He details two types of muru'a: at home (Quran recitation, mosque attendance, helping brothers, treating servants well) and while travelling (sharing provisions, keeping secrets, appropriate humor). He concludes by swearing that Allah provides sustenance, aid, and patience in proportion to one's manliness, expenditure, and affliction respectively.
